name: DecoBlocks
author: LUX Digest

sections.description:
Most WordPress posts read like documents. DecoBlocks is built for the posts that should read like you — the ones where a reader stops scrolling, actually feels something, and sticks around.

Plain, information-only writing is easy to skim, easy to summarize, and increasingly easy to replace. What’s harder to replace is a post with a real voice behind it — the small human touches (a sticker at just the right moment, a highlighted aside, a speech bubble that sounds like you talking) that no template and no AI-generated draft quite gets right. That’s the gap DecoBlocks fills: the same kind of expressive stickers you already use every day in chat apps, brought into your blog posts — a visual rhythm for pacing emotion across a page that WordPress has never quite had.

The practical effect, when it’s used well: readers stay on the page longer, they’re more likely to comment or come back, and your writing simply feels more like someone’s, not something’s. DecoBlocks doesn’t promise a ranking boost — no plugin honestly can — but posts that keep people reading and coming back are exactly the kind of signal search engines are built to reward.

Character stickers are the centerpiece: install packs made by independent illustrators (Insert Sticker block, or the Get from Marketplace tab) and drop them into your posts to punctuate a feeling — surprise, warmth, a laugh — the same way a well-placed sticker does on a personal blog. Alongside them, DecoBlocks gives you a full set of ready-made design blocks — speech bubbles, styled quote boxes, section boxes, custom bullet icons, text highlights, an auto-generated table of contents, glow effects, and an animated firework decoration — all without writing a single line of CSS, as native blocks (Gutenberg) or shortcodes (Classic Editor).

Whether you call it post decoration, blog design, writing decoration, or content styling, DecoBlocks is built to make your posts beautiful, readable, and — most of all — recognizably, humanly yours.

Free Features

  • Speech bubble (filled / outline, left/right)
  • Section box (solid / shadow / dashed)
  • Custom bullet list icons (check / star / heart / arrow / point)
  • Text highlight (yellow / green)
  • Auto-generated table of contents
  • Sparkle text effect
  • Glow box (pulse effect)
  • Auto-repeating firework decoration (gold / rainbow colors, adjustable particle count and timing)
  • Quote block with multiple built-in styles (classic / vertical bar / line frame / big quotation marks / sticky note / corner frame – the last two show a plain, undecorated version for free; the colored, decorated version needs the 3D Style Upgrade)
  • Speech bubble Pastel style (plain gray version for free; the colored pastel + avatar image needs the 3D Style Upgrade)
  • Glow box Twinkle style (glows the same as Pulse Glow for free; the sparkling star decoration needs the 3D Style Upgrade)
  • Divider block with multiple built-in styles (solid / dashed / dotted / diamond / arrow / diagonal slash / tick mark – the last four show a plain, undecorated version for free; the gradient, shadowed version needs the 3D Style Upgrade)
  • Custom color palette and the option to hide the “Powered by” credit — both free, no upgrade needed
  • Independent heading tag (H2–H6, or plain text) and font size choice on every text block — your choice, whether or not you want it picked up by search engines
  • Works in both the Block Editor and the Classic Editor

3D Style Upgrade (paid add-on)

  • Pastel speech bubble style and avatar images
  • Sticky-note and corner-frame quote styles
  • Diamond / arrow / diagonal-slash / tick-mark divider ornaments
  • Multi-color confetti firework bursts
  • Rainbow shine text, glowing twinkle-star box, and animated gradient highlight sweep
  • Genuine 3D depth effects (shadows, embossing, elevation) layered on top of the styles above

External services

This plugin connects to a marketplace server operated by the plugin author (store.luxdigest.com) for the optional sticker-pack feature. No data is sent to this server as part of normal plugin use (decoration blocks, shortcodes, TOC, etc.) — only the specific actions below trigger a connection, and only when you actively use them:

  • Browsing/installing sticker packs (“Get from Marketplace” tab in the Insert Sticker block): sends your site’s language (ko/en/ja, informational only — the server returns every pack regardless) and, when installing a pack, your license key and site URL (home_url()), to fetch the pack list and download the pack’s image files. Endpoints: GET /packs, GET /packs/{slug} — used only when you open this tab or click Install.
  • Sticker pack license lookup (DecoBlocks → License Keys): sends the license key you paste to identify which pack it belongs to, then reuses the pack install flow above. Endpoint: GET /license-lookup — used only when you click “Add”.
  • Purchase links: the “Get 3D Styles” and pack purchase buttons link out (in a new browser tab) to /buy-3d and /buy/{slug} on the same marketplace server to complete a purchase. No data is sent automatically — this only opens when you click a purchase button yourself.

The DecoBlocks 3D Style Upgrade is a separate, independent plugin, not distributed through WordPress.org — this free plugin never downloads, installs, or connects to anything on its behalf. It is sold directly on store.luxdigest.com; after purchase you receive an email with a link to download the plugin’s zip file, which you install manually like any other plugin (Plugins → Add New → Upload Plugin). All license verification for that upgrade happens inside that separate plugin, not here.

This service is operated by the same developer as this plugin. Terms of Service: https://store.luxdigest.com/terms-of-service/ — Privacy Policy: https://store.luxdigest.com/privacy-policy/ — Refund Policy: https://store.luxdigest.com/refund-policy/ — Contact: https://store.luxdigest.com/contact/
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin files to /wp-content/plugins/decoblocks, or install the plugin through the WordPress plugins screen directly.
  2. Activate the plugin through the ‘Plugins’ screen in WordPress.
  3. Look for the “DecoBlocks” category in the block inserter, or use the toolbar buttons in the Classic Editor.
sections.faq:
Does this work with the Classic Editor?

Yes. Every block also has a matching shortcode with a toolbar button and Quicktags button for the Classic Editor.

Will this slow down my site?

No. Styles and scripts are only loaded when needed, and all animations are lightweight, dependency-free JavaScript.
sections.changelog:
2.44.32

  • Added: Glow Box 3D’s multi-color rainbow pulse is no longer the only “3D” look. A new “3D Glow Color” dropdown (shown once the 3D preview is turned on) lets you choose between “Use My Color” (default) and “Rainbow”. “Use My Color” makes the glow a single-hue neon effect built from whatever color you’ve picked for the box – pick red, the glow is red; pick purple, the glow is purple – layered at a few different blur/opacity levels for a genuine neon-sign look, instead of always being a fixed multi-color rainbow. If the box’s color is left at its default black, the 3D glow falls back to a bright orange instead of a barely-visible black glow. “Rainbow” keeps the existing gold/orange/green cycling glow from 2.44.31 for anyone who prefers it. Also available in the Classic Editor shortcode as [decobl_glow rainbow3d="1"].

2.44.31

  • Fixed: Quote Box – Classic’s 3D preview added a whole-element ambient shadow in 2.44.30 to connect the shading through the middle, but each bracket end (::before/::after) still kept its own separate drop shadow on top of that, so the two brackets visually “floated” one layer above the box beneath them instead of reading as one continuous surface. Removed the brackets’ own individual box-shadow – their light/dark top-to-bottom border coloring is enough on its own, layered under the single whole-element shadow, so it now reads as one consistent raised surface end to end.
  • Redesigned: Glow Box 3D’s gold/orange/green glow (2.44.30) only ever changed in brightness, never in color balance – all three color layers grew and shrank together at the exact same ratio, so the closest/brightest gold layer always visually dominated and the whole effect just read as “a fixed yellow glow,” not a rainbow. The pulse animation is rebuilt so each color takes a turn being the largest, brightest layer in a rotating sequence (gold → orange → green → back to gold), so the glow now visibly shifts between colors over time instead of only pulsing in intensity. Animation length increased from 2s to 3s so the color shift reads as a smooth transition rather than a flicker.

2.44.30

  • Fixed: Quote Box – Classic’s 3D preview only shaded the two bracket ends (::before/::after) – the flat area between them (where the quote text sits) had no shading at all, so the box read as “raised only at both edges, flat in the middle” instead of one continuously lifted shape. Added a soft ambient box-shadow to the element itself (on top of the brackets’ own existing shading), so the whole quote box now reads as a single continuously raised surface, brackets included.
  • Fixed: Quote Box – Vertical Bar’s 3D bar still showed a hint of black at its base even after 2.44.27’s color-mix() fix, because the gradient’s darkest stop was mixed 60% color / 40% black – dark enough to read as near-black on lower-saturation colors – and the bar’s own ambient drop shadow was strong enough to visually blend into that dark end. Lightened the gradient’s dark stop to 78% color / 22% black and softened the ambient shadow, so the bar’s base now reads as a darker shade of the chosen color instead of black bleeding through.
  • Changed: Glow Box 3D’s rainbow pulse used a pink/purple/teal palette that read as dark and muddy rather than a true “rainbow” glow. Replaced with a brighter gold/orange/green combination (the green matches the plugin’s own default accent color for consistency), matching the warmer, brighter palette originally intended for this effect.

2.44.29

  • Changed: the block inserter’s item names now show this plugin’s internal CSS block-reference number instead of the generic “(DecoBlocks)” suffix – e.g. “Speech Bubble (1-1-1)” for the free version and “✨ Speech Bubble (1-1-2, 3D)” for its 3D preview, “Quote Box – Classic (10-1-1)” / “(10-1-2, 3D)”, and so on for every block. This is purely a label change for easier reference between the block list and the CSS source (assets/css/dbk-frontend.css is organized under matching numbered comment headers, e.g. “10-1-1″/”10-1-2”) – no rendering, styling, or attribute behavior changed. The “Purchase Required to Publish” notice on unlicensed 3D items is unchanged, just now prefixed with its reference number.

2.44.28

  • Fixed: Section Box and Glow Box’s “Title” field could never actually become a real H2-H6 heading, even though the block’s Typography panel let you choose a heading tag for the body content. The title itself was always hard-coded to render as a plain <div> (in both the PHP renderer and the block editor’s own preview), so the Table of Contents block – which scans the page’s real HTML for <h2>/<h3> tags – could never pick it up, no matter what a writer intended the title to be. Added a dedicated “Title heading level” dropdown (Default / H2 / H3 / H4 / H5 / H6) that appears once a title is entered, for both Section Box and Glow Box, in the block editor, and wired the same option into the [decobl_box title_tag="h2"] / [decobl_glow title_tag="h2"] Classic Editor shortcodes. Titles marked H2 or H3 are now automatically picked up by the Table of Contents block, exactly like any other H2/H3 in the post. Leaving this at its default keeps rendering a plain, non-heading <div> exactly as before, so already-published posts are unaffected. Also added a margin: 0 reset to the title’s CSS so switching it to a real heading tag doesn’t introduce the browser’s default heading margin around it.

2.44.27

  • Redesigned: Quote Box – Classic’s box-with-a-border shape from 2.44.26 turned out to be visually indistinguishable from Section Box’s own plain rectangle. Rebuilt as a pair of classic open bracket shapes (“[” on the left, “]” on the right, each a 3-sided corner stroke) wrapping the quote text instead – a silhouette that doesn’t overlap with Section Box, Vertical Bar, or the Big Quotation Marks style. 3D keeps this exact bracket shape and only shades it (lighter top edge, darker bottom edge, soft drop shadow).
  • Redesigned: Quote Box – Vertical Bar’s 3D preview now also lifts the entire quote box with a soft shadow (the same technique used for Section Box/Classic), in addition to keeping its own bar – previously only the bar itself got extra shading, not the box around it.
  • Fixed: Quote Box – Vertical Bar’s 3D bar showed a visible black tint mixed into the color whenever a non-default (non-black) quote color was chosen, because the light/shadow effect was built from separate white/black translucent overlay layers stacked on top of the color. Rebuilt using color-mix() (the same technique already used for the Highlight gradient) so the bar is a single continuous shade of the chosen color, light to dark, with no separate black layer showing through. The bar’s outer black ring outline is also removed for the same reason; only an ordinary ambient drop shadow (which is expected to be dark regardless of the element’s own color) remains.
  • Fixed: Glow Box 3D’s multi-color pulsing glow was still shown next to the plain single-color border from the free-tier style (which defaults to black), making the two look disconnected. The border is now hidden (made transparent, same box size) whenever the 3D preview is active, so only the glow itself defines the edge.

2.44.26

  • Redesigned: Quote Box – Classic’s free/base shape was still a single left border, which didn’t visually read as a distinct style from Quote Box – Vertical Bar and made the two hard to tell apart at a glance. The base style itself is now a bordered box on all four sides (not just a left edge) – this is an explicit, user-directed change to the free-tier CSS (normally left alone). The 3D preview keeps this exact same box shape and only adds soft light/shadow depth on top of it – no separate accent bar, and no decorative quotation-mark glyphs (removed – they duplicated the dedicated Quotation Marks style and weren’t wanted here).
  • Fixed: Quote Box – Line Frame’s 3D top/bottom lines sat flush against the box’s own padding edge, which read as neither clearly attached nor clearly floating (“어정쩡한” was the word used). The lines are now offset 6px outward from the box, giving them visible breathing room from the quote text so they read as a deliberate floating frame instead of an ambiguous half-border.
  • Changed: Quote Box – Sticky Note’s free/base background was an almost-white pale gray (#F8F7F2) meant to be a deliberately muted placeholder – but it read as “neither colored nor uncolored,” an ambiguous half-measure rather than an intentional design choice. Replaced with a clearly visible pastel yellow (#FFF3B0) so the free version unmistakably looks like a sticky note; the 3D preview’s richer gradient still builds naturally on top of it.

2.44.25

  • Restructured: dbk-frontend.css is reorganized into a numbered block scheme (e.g. 1-1-1/1-1-2 for Speech Bubble’s free/3D pair, 10-1-1/10-1-2 for Quote – Classic’s free/3D pair, and so on) so that every element’s free-tier CSS sits immediately next to its own 3D CSS, instead of free styles living in one part of the file and all 3D styles being grouped together at the end. This is a structural change only – no CSS class name was renamed (blocks-editor.js’s class-name dependencies are untouched), and the free/3D editor-only switch continues to work exactly as before via .editor-styles-wrapper. The goal is to make it structurally harder to accidentally reuse one generic 3D treatment across visually distinct named styles, and to make it obvious, block by block, which CSS is free (editor + published) and which is 3D-preview-only (editor only, until the paid 3D Style Upgrade is installed and licensed).
  • Redesigned: Quote Box – Classic’s 3D preview still read as “Vertical Bar with square corners” because its left border bar was left in place. The 3D-only rule now removes that left bar entirely (the free/base style’s border-left is untouched), turns the whole element into an actual bordered box with soft light/shadow depth, and adds a small classic-style opening/closing quotation mark in the top-left and bottom-right corners – so Classic is now visually its own shape, not a variant of Vertical Bar’s silhouette.
  • Fixed: Quote Box – Line Frame’s 3D preview still looked like one thick merged bar even after being reduced to a 3px-tall line in 2.44.23. The actual cause wasn’t the height – it was a box-shadow blur sitting on top of the line that visually spread past its edges and made it read as bulkier than its real height. The blur is removed and the line height is reduced once more (2px), so the top/bottom lines now render as genuinely thin, crisp strokes with the light/dark emboss built into the line itself rather than a shadow around it.
  • Strengthened: Quote Box – Vertical Bar’s 3D preview wasn’t reading as dimensional enough, especially against the plugin’s default black quote color – the highlight/shadow gradient on the bar was too subtle to notice. Contrast is substantially increased (the same fix already applied to Speech Bubble and Section Box in 2.44.23), and a thin dark outline plus inner edge highlight were added so the bar’s own silhouette stays legible even on black.
  • Cleanup: removed the @keyframes dbk-glow-pulse animation definition and its prefers-reduced-motion override – both became dead code once Glow Box’s free-tier pulse/twinkle animation was removed in 2.44.24 (nothing in the stylesheet referenced them anymore).

2.44.24

  • Fixed: Speech Bubble 3D’s “✨” corner badge was implemented as an ::after pseudo-element, but the bubble’s own speech-bubble tail (.dbk-bubble--left/--right.dbk-bubble--filled/--outline::after) already uses ::after for its triangle – an element can only have one ::after, so the higher-specificity 3D rule completely replaced the tail with the badge instead of the two coexisting. This is what showed up as a stray shape where the tail should be. The badge is removed; the tail is intact again, and the bubble’s depth still reads clearly from its shadow/gloss alone.
  • Redesigned: Section Box and Quote Box – Classic’s 3D still wasn’t reading as genuine depth – Section Box’s hard-edged solid-color double ring looked like “a thick black line,” not shading, and Classic’s overlaid bar was functionally the same technique as Vertical Bar’s own bar (just square instead of round), so the two didn’t feel distinct as promised. Both are rebuilt around soft, blurred light/shadow only (a pale near-white glow, a graduated drop shadow, an inset highlight) applied to the entire box, with no hard color ring and no bar element – Classic’s own border-left is left completely untouched, and Section Box no longer resembles Vertical Bar’s silhouette at all.
  • Fixed: Highlight 3D’s gradient ran the wrong direction for how a highlighter stroke reads left-to-right, and was tilted off-axis (100deg). It’s now a clean 90deg gradient, darker at the left and lightening toward the right.
  • Fixed: Glow Box – the base (free) Pulse and Twinkle styles animated even though only the 3D version is supposed to. Both base styles are now static (steady glow, no animation) – only the 3D version pulses.
  • Redesigned: Glow Box 3D’s rainbow was cycling through one solid hue at a time, which read as “a single color blinking,” not “rainbow.” It now layers three hues (pink/purple/teal) as simultaneous, overlapping glows that all breathe together, so multiple colors are visibly present at once.
  • Fixed: Sticky Note 3D leaned on its color change to signal “3D,” but the sticky note’s base version is already colored – repeating that the base already has color and 3D should intensify the depth on top of it. Its highlight/shadow layering is now much stronger (a real “the paper is lifting” look) while the color itself stays the same as before.

2.44.23

  • Fixed: Speech Bubble and Section Box 3D’s light/shadow signal was too subtle to notice at all against the default black color (confirmed by real screenshots showing no visible difference from the base version) – depth shadows and highlights are now much stronger and clearly visible regardless of the color chosen.
  • Fixed: Section Box’s 3D treatment (a left accent bar) looked almost identical to Quote Box – Vertical Bar’s own left bar, making the two indistinguishable in the editor (direct user feedback, twice). Section Box no longer uses a side bar at all – it now gets a raised double-ring frame around its whole border instead, which reads as “a box/frame,” not “a bar,” so it no longer converges with Vertical Bar’s silhouette.
  • Fixed: Line Frame’s 3D lines were thickened to 5px in 2.44.22 to fix the previous “too thin” bug, but that overshot into a blunt, merged-looking double band instead of the intended “two thin lines” (confirmed by screenshot). Reduced back to 3px (in line with the base version’s own weight) while keeping the glossy light/shadow finish.
  • Fixed: Glow Box 3D reusing the box’s own single configured color (per the “don’t invent a new color” rule applied elsewhere) made it nearly invisible whenever that color was the default black, and made it indistinguishable from the base version’s own already-existing subtle pulse. Per direct feedback, Glow Box is a deliberate exception to the “reuse existing color” rule – its 3D identity is specifically a colorful, multi-hue pulsing glow (unrelated to the picked border color), which is restored here using box-shadow only (not the background-clip trick that caused the corner-banding bug in 2.44.21).
  • Fixed: Highlight 3D still used a fixed 4-color gradient (yellow/pink/purple/teal) that ignored the “Gradient Color” picked in the sidebar – “a gradient means one color getting lighter or darker, not several unrelated colors side by side” (direct feedback). It’s now a genuine single-hue gradient built entirely from the picked --dbk-highlight-gradient-color (lighter tint to the picked color to a darker shade of the same color, using color-mix(), with a flat-color fallback for older browsers) – no fixed color is used anywhere in it.

2.44.22

  • Fixed: Line Frame’s 3D version used border-image for the gradient top/bottom lines – it rendered thinner and fainter than the plain base version instead of thicker (a visible regression, confirmed by screenshot). border-image is no longer used anywhere in this file; Line Frame’s 3D lines are now drawn as solid overlaid bars instead, guaranteed to render as intended across browsers.
  • Fixed: Highlight 3D’s gradient start color was hardcoded to #F5C400 in 2.44.21, silently ignoring the sidebar’s “Gradient Color” swatch (blocks-editor.js was already correctly writing the chosen color into --dbk-highlight-gradient-color – only the CSS had stopped reading it). Restored to read that variable, exactly as it worked in 2.44.18.
  • Fixed: Glow Box 3D’s gradient border (background-clip: padding-box, border-box trick) rendered as visibly disconnected color bands at the corners instead of a smooth border, and was nearly invisible in the inserter’s small hover-preview thumbnail. Replaced with a box-shadow-based glow in the block’s own already-configured color – renders smoothly at any size and is far more visible at thumbnail scale since blur naturally reads better small than a 2px gradient border does.
  • Redesigned (per direct feedback: “a color change is not what ‘3D’ means – real depth comes from light and shadow, not hue, and it has to stay consistent with whatever color I already picked”): every remaining 3D rule for Speech Bubble, Section Box, Quote Box (all 6 sub-styles), and Divider (all 7 sub-styles) now reads and reuses that element’s own existing color variable (--dbk-bubble-color, --dbk-box-color, --dbk-quote-color, --dbk-divider-color) instead of a fixed decorative palette, and expresses “3D” purely through layered light/shadow (translucent white highlight + translucent black shadow, plus card-elevation drop shadows and embossed text-shadow on glyphs) – never by introducing a new color the user didn’t choose. Each of the 6 quote sub-styles and 7 divider sub-styles still gets its own distinct rule built on its own existing element (no two share a rule), per the redesign in 2.44.21, but none of them recolor what the user already set.
  • Postit’s 3D preview now shows the actual intended postit-yellow color and paper sheen directly (not a muted placeholder) – the “free preview, purchase required to publish” model means the editor preview should show the real result in full; only the published/live post is what’s gated behind purchase.

2.44.21

  • Fixed: the 2.44.20 revert (see below) went too far – reverting blocks-editor.js wholesale to the 2.44.16 original also undid the Firework Effect icon fix from 2.44.18 (its icon collided with Glow Box’s icon, and its 3D-variant icon collided with Sparkle Text’s icon). That collision is back to being fixed: both the base and 3D-variant Firework Effect entries use their own dedicated icon again, restored exactly as in 2.44.18. Also restored the window.DECOBL_FIREWORK_COLORS.confetti3d palette hook (editor-only, from 2.44.18) so the Firework Effect’s “Multi-Color Burst (3D)” preview actually bursts in real colors instead of silently falling back to gold.
  • Redesigned: all “3D preview” CSS, from scratch, to fix the actual design complaint behind the 2.44.20 revert – not “no visual difference” (2.44.16), and not “one identical colored frame/bar reused everywhere” (2.44.17-19), but a distinct treatment per block/style that builds on that style’s own existing visual element:
    • Quote Box (6 styles): Classic’s own left border becomes a gradient border; Vertical Bar’s own bar gets thicker + gradient + glow; Line Frame’s own top/bottom lines become gradient borders; Big Quotation Marks’ own “curly quote” glyphs get a gradient fill; Sticky Note gets an actual pastel-yellow tint plus a folded-corner triangle; Corner Frame’s own 4 corner brackets get thicker + gradient colors. No two of these six share a CSS rule.
    • Divider (7 styles): Solid gets a smooth 3-color gradient bar; Dashed gets thick 3-color repeating dash segments; Dotted gets alternating two-color dots with a slow drift animation; Diamond keeps its own ◆ glyph but fills it with a gradient and fades the line at both ends; Arrow keeps its own glyph with a soft glow and a gentle bounce; Slash’s own bar gets thicker + gradient + glow; Tick gets its own bar thickened plus two smaller flanking ticks for a “measurement cluster” look. No two of these seven share a CSS rule or look alike.
    • Speech Bubble / Section Box: share one coherent glossy-highlight-plus-depth-shadow treatment (their 3 sub-styles differ only by fill color/border, not by shape, so one physically-consistent “premium” finish is applied consistently rather than each getting an unrelated custom design) plus a small in-bounds sparkle marker.
    • Glow Box / Sparkle Text / Custom Bullet List / Highlight keep their existing bespoke 3D classes from 2.44.19 (each was already block-specific, never shared across block types, and was not part of what was reported as looking generic).
  • All rules stay under .editor-styles-wrapper (editor-only, confirmed working) and stay fully inside each element’s own box (inset shadows, background-clip: text, border-image, small in-bounds pseudo-elements) – nothing relies on box-shadow/filter bleeding outside the block, which is what the inserter’s hover-preview panel was confirmed to clip in 2.44.19.

2.44.20

  • Reverted: all “3D preview” CSS/JS added in 2.44.17-2.44.19 (.dbk-3d-premium, .dbk-glow--rainbow3d, .dbk-sparkle--rainbow3d, .dbk-bullet-list--rainbow3d, .dbk-highlight--gradient3d, .dbk-divider--3d, plus the related firework icon/color additions in blocks-editor.js) has been fully removed. assets/css/dbk-frontend.css and assets/js/blocks-editor.js are now byte-for-byte identical to the 2.44.16 originals.
  • Why: three separate attempts (2.44.17, 2.44.18, 2.44.19) at giving the free plugin’s “3D preview” a distinct editor-only look were each visually wrong in a different way (destroyed the base style’s own look, a generic colored frame/ring slapped on top regardless of block type, and – worst – one single uniform treatment applied identically across all 7 divider sub-styles, erasing the point of having separate named styles at all). Rather than ship a fourth guess, the older reference file provided (2.44.15) was checked directly: it contains no real 3D visual CSS either – the actual 3D artwork has only ever existed in the separate paid “3D Style Upgrade” add-on, never in this free plugin at any version. Inventing a substitute in the free plugin was the wrong approach from the start, so it has been removed rather than patched again.
  • Net effect: 3D preview items in the inserter behave exactly as they did in 2.44.16 – visually identical to their base counterpart in the editor, distinguished only by their name/label and the “purchase required to publish” tooltip. No other file in the plugin was touched (verified by diff -rq against the original upload: only dbk-frontend.css, blocks-editor.js, decoblocks.php and this readme differ).

2.44.19

  • Fixed: after 2.44.18, real editor screenshots still showed several 3D previews (Speech Bubble, Section Box, Quote Box – all styles, Glow Box) looking the same as their base version. Root cause: .dbk-3d-premium‘s corner badge and .dbk-glow--rainbow3d‘s twinkle-star decorations were positioned with negative offsets (deliberately hanging slightly outside the block’s own box, e.g. top: -11px) and their glow used an outward box-shadow/filter: drop-shadow(...) – all of which extend past the block’s own edges. The inserter’s hover-preview panel fits each preview into a small fixed box and very plausibly clips anything that extends past that box’s edges, so all of it could be getting silently cut off there even though it renders fine in the full-size editor canvas. Every 3D indicator for these blocks now stays entirely inside the block’s own boundary: the border ring and glow are inset box-shadows (which by definition can never render outside the element), and the corner badge/twinkle stars are positioned inside the box instead of overlapping its edge – so nothing here depends on whether the preview panel clips overflowing content.

2.44.18

  • Fixed: 2.44.17’s fix for the 3D preview classes was itself broken for several blocks, confirmed against real editor screenshots. .dbk-3d-premium (Speech Bubble, Section Box, and all six Quote Box styles) used a background-image gradient-border trick that silently replaced any background/background-image the underlying style already had – so Quote Box – Sticky Note lost its cream postit color entirely and Quote Box – Corner Frame lost its gradient corner-bracket decoration, both collapsing into a plain white box. Replaced it with a purely additive treatment (a filter: drop-shadow(...) glow plus a small “✨ 3D” corner badge as its own ::after element) that never touches background, border, or box-shadow on the block itself, so every style keeps its own real look underneath, whatever it already was.
  • Fixed: the Highlight 3D preview (.dbk-highlight--gradient3d) technically used a gradient, but it only faded to transparent in the last 10% of the text width, so on short sample text it read as one flat color – indistinguishable from just picking a different highlight color. It now uses the same highlighter-bar shape as the free Yellow/Green styles (color filling the bottom ~40% of the line) but with the color itself running through the chosen Gradient Color into the brand accent colors across the full width, so it reads as a gradient at a glance.
  • Fixed: the Firework Effect block’s base icon was lightbulb – identical to the unrelated Glow Box block’s icon – while its own “(3D)” variation used star-filled, identical to the unrelated Sparkle Text block’s icon. Two different blocks shared one icon each, and Firework Effect’s own base/3D pair didn’t even match each other, so nothing in the inserter’s icons reliably told these blocks apart or showed which entries were variations of the same block. Firework Effect now has its own dedicated icon (a small multi-color burst), used identically for both its base and 3D entries.

2.44.17

  • Fixed: the “(3D — Purchase Required to Publish)” inserter entries for every 3D-capable block (Speech Bubble, Section Box, Highlight, Sparkle Text, Glow Box, Firework Effect, Custom Bullet List / Checklist, all six Quote Box styles, all seven Divider styles) looked visually identical to their plain counterparts, both in the inserter’s hover preview and inside the block itself while editing — even though the JS side was correctly applying the is3d/3D attribute and its CSS class the whole time. The root cause: this free plugin’s own stylesheet never actually defined the classes those 3D toggles switch on (.dbk-3d-premium, .dbk-glow--rainbow3d, .dbk-sparkle--rainbow3d, .dbk-bullet-list--rainbow3d, .dbk-highlight--gradient3d, .dbk-divider--3d) — every one of them was left entirely to the paid 3D Style Upgrade add-on, so without it there was nothing to render any visible difference at all, contradicting the inserter’s own tooltip text (“This is a free preview shown in the editor only”). Added a real free-tier preview design (gradient border/glow, rainbow shine, twinkle stars, gradient bullet icon, gradient highlight, gradient divider bar) for every one of these classes, scoped with the .editor-styles-wrapper selector prefix so it only ever renders inside the Block Editor (main canvas and inserter preview alike) and never on the published front-end — sites without the add-on still see exactly the same plain output on the live page as before, preserving the reason to purchase the upgrade.
  • Fixed: the Firework Effect block’s “(3D)” preview (colors: 'confetti3d') silently fell back to the plain gold burst in the editor, for the same reason — window.DECOBL_FIREWORK_COLORS.confetti3d was only ever populated by the paid add-on. The block editor script now fills in its own free preview-only rainbow palette for confetti3d (only when the object doesn’t already have one, so it never overrides the real add-on’s colors on sites that have it installed). Since this script is only ever loaded on the editor screen (enqueue_block_editor_assets), the published front-end – where dbk-firework.js is loaded alone – is completely unaffected and still requires the add-on for a real multi-color burst.
  • No changes to the block markup, attributes, or PHP render output – only editor-scoped CSS/JS were added, so this only changes what the editor preview looks like, not what’s already saved in the database or how it’s ever rendered on a published page.

2.44.16

  • Fixed: on several blocks (Quote Box – Sticky Note / Corner Frame, Speech Bubble – Pastel, Glow Box – Twinkle, Divider – Diamond/Arrow/Diagonal Slash/Tick Mark), choosing the style itself – independently of the separate “3D Premium Frame” star toggle – silently depended on the paid 3D Style Upgrade add-on’s CSS for any visible design. Without the add-on, these styles rendered as either nothing but bare padding or, for the four divider ornament styles, a misplaced/broken-looking decoration, even though nothing was actually wrong – it just looked broken. Each of these now has its own real, complete free-tier design (kept visibly simpler than the paid version, so the upgrade still has a reason to exist) that renders correctly with or without the add-on.
  • Fixed: the same styles gave no warning of any kind in the editor when the paid add-on was installed but not licensed (a very common state, since the add-on always shows the true 3D-styled look in the editor regardless of license, by design – see the add-on’s own enqueue_editor()) – so the block would look fully decorated while editing but silently fall back to plain on publish, with no explanation anywhere. Every one of these style choices now shows the same clear “🔒 preview only, purchase required to publish” notice already used by the “3D Premium Frame” toggle, whether or not that toggle itself is on.
  • No changes to the block markup or existing published post content – only CSS/JS were touched, and PHP output is unchanged, so this only affects future edits/re-renders, not what’s already saved in the database.

2.44.15

  • Fixed: quote blocks (Classic, Vertical Bar, Line Frame, Big Quotation Marks, Sticky Note, Corner Frame) could render with almost no inner padding and less vertical margin than intended on the published page, even though the Block Editor preview looked correct. Verified directly against a live site (luxdigest.com): each quote block is a real <blockquote> element, and many themes attach their own default blockquote look with a selector like .entry-content blockquote — one class plus the blockquote tag. That selector’s specificity is higher than this plugin’s own single-class .dbk-quote--line-frame-style padding rules, and the theme’s stylesheet is enqueued after this plugin’s, so on ties the theme wins the cascade outright — the plugin’s border rules already carried !important for exactly this reason (added in an earlier fix), but the padding and outer margin rules did not, so …

short_description: Writing that expresses real human emotion — DecoBlocks turns it into something cooler, more fun, and more lovable.
description:
Most WordPress posts read like documents. DecoBlocks is built for the posts that should read like you — the ones where a reader stops scrolling, actually feels something, and sticks around.

Plain, information-only writing is easy to skim, easy to summarize, and increasingly easy to replace. What’s harder to replace is a post with a real voice behind it — the small human touches (a sticker at just the right moment, a highlighted aside, a speech bubble that sounds like you talking) that no template and no AI-generated draft quite gets right. That’s the gap DecoBlocks fills: the same kind of expressive stickers you already use every day in chat apps, brought into your blog posts — a visual rhythm for pacing emotion across a page that WordPress has never quite had.

The practical effect, when it’s used well: readers stay on the page longer, they’re more likely to comment or come back, and your writing simply feels more like someone’s, not something’s. DecoBlocks doesn’t promise a ranking boost — no plugin honestly can — but posts that keep people reading and coming back are exactly the kind of signal search engines are built to reward.

Character stickers are the centerpiece: install packs made by independent illustrators (Insert Sticker block, or the Get from Marketplace tab) and drop them into your posts to punctuate a feeling — surprise, warmth, a laugh — the same way a well-placed sticker does on a personal blog. Alongside them, DecoBlocks gives you a full set of ready-made design blocks — speech bubbles, styled quote boxes, section boxes, custom bullet icons, text highlights, an auto-generated table of contents, glow effects, and an animated firework decoration — all without writing a single line of CSS, as native blocks (Gutenberg) or shortcodes (Classic Editor).

Whether you call it post decoration, blog design, writing decoration, or content styling, DecoBlocks is built to make your posts beautiful, readable, and — most of all — recognizably, humanly yours.

Free Features

  • Speech bubble (filled / outline, left/right)
  • Section box (solid / shadow / dashed)
  • Custom bullet list icons (check / star / heart / arrow / point)
  • Text highlight (yellow / green)
  • Auto-generated table of contents
  • Sparkle text effect
  • Glow box (pulse effect)
  • Auto-repeating firework decoration (gold / rainbow colors, adjustable particle count and timing)
  • Quote block with multiple built-in styles (classic / vertical bar / line frame / big quotation marks / sticky note / corner frame – the last two show a plain, undecorated version for free; the colored, decorated version needs the 3D Style Upgrade)
  • Speech bubble Pastel style (plain gray version for free; the colored pastel + avatar image needs the 3D Style Upgrade)
  • Glow box Twinkle style (glows the same as Pulse Glow for free; the sparkling star decoration needs the 3D Style Upgrade)
  • Divider block with multiple built-in styles (solid / dashed / dotted / diamond / arrow / diagonal slash / tick mark – the last four show a plain, undecorated version for free; the gradient, shadowed version needs the 3D Style Upgrade)
  • Custom color palette and the option to hide the “Powered by” credit — both free, no upgrade needed
  • Independent heading tag (H2–H6, or plain text) and font size choice on every text block — your choice, whether or not you want it picked up by search engines
  • Works in both the Block Editor and the Classic Editor

3D Style Upgrade (paid add-on)

  • Pastel speech bubble style and avatar images
  • Sticky-note and corner-frame quote styles
  • Diamond / arrow / diagonal-slash / tick-mark divider ornaments
  • Multi-color confetti firework bursts
  • Rainbow shine text, glowing twinkle-star box, and animated gradient highlight sweep
  • Genuine 3D depth effects (shadows, embossing, elevation) layered on top of the styles above

External services

This plugin connects to a marketplace server operated by the plugin author (store.luxdigest.com) for the optional sticker-pack feature. No data is sent to this server as part of normal plugin use (decoration blocks, shortcodes, TOC, etc.) — only the specific actions below trigger a connection, and only when you actively use them:

  • Browsing/installing sticker packs (“Get from Marketplace” tab in the Insert Sticker block): sends your site’s language (ko/en/ja, informational only — the server returns every pack regardless) and, when installing a pack, your license key and site URL (home_url()), to fetch the pack list and download the pack’s image files. Endpoints: GET /packs, GET /packs/{slug} — used only when you open this tab or click Install.
  • Sticker pack license lookup (DecoBlocks → License Keys): sends the license key you paste to identify which pack it belongs to, then reuses the pack install flow above. Endpoint: GET /license-lookup — used only when you click “Add”.
  • Purchase links: the “Get 3D Styles” and pack purchase buttons link out (in a new browser tab) to /buy-3d and /buy/{slug} on the same marketplace server to complete a purchase. No data is sent automatically — this only opens when you click a purchase button yourself.

The DecoBlocks 3D Style Upgrade is a separate, independent plugin, not distributed through WordPress.org — this free plugin never downloads, installs, or connects to anything on its behalf. It is sold directly on store.luxdigest.com; after purchase you receive an email with a link to download the plugin’s zip file, which you install manually like any other plugin (Plugins → Add New → Upload Plugin). All license verification for that upgrade happens inside that separate plugin, not here.

This service is operated by the same developer as this plugin. Terms of Service: https://store.luxdigest.com/terms-of-service/ — Privacy Policy: https://store.luxdigest.com/privacy-policy/ — Refund Policy: https://store.luxdigest.com/refund-policy/ — Contact: https://store.luxdigest.com/contact/
